7-1.title: Building the Pyramids
7-1.learn:
KEY IDEAS — BUILDING THE PYRAMIDS

The Egyptians built enormous stone PYRAMIDS as TOMBS for their pharaohs. The pyramids were giant burial places meant to protect the pharaoh's body and treasures and to help the pharaoh reach the afterlife. The most famous is the Great Pyramid at Giza, the largest pyramid of all, built for the pharaoh Khufu. It is one of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World and still stands today.

Building a pyramid was an incredible task. Thousands of skilled workers cut, moved, and stacked huge blocks of stone, some weighing many tons, with amazing precision. They used ramps, levers, and careful planning, lining the pyramid up almost perfectly with the directions of the compass.

The pyramids show off Egypt's incredible ENGINEERING, MATH, and ORGANIZATION. To build something so huge and exact, Egyptians needed advanced geometry, skilled architects, and a government strong enough to organize thousands of workers and supplies. The pyramids prove how advanced and well-organized ancient Egyptian civilization really was. Remember: pyramids = Egyptian tombs.

questions.question: Which tools did the Egyptians use to help move and lift the heavy stone blocks?

questions.question: Compared to a small grave, a pyramid shows that a pharaoh was viewed as what?

questions.question: Put these in order from first to last: a pharaoh dies, a pyramid tomb is built, the pharaoh's body is protected inside.

7-2.title: Hieroglyphics and Egyptian Achievements
7-2.learn:
KEY IDEAS — HIEROGLYPHICS AND EGYPTIAN ACHIEVEMENTS

The Egyptians created their own picture-writing system called HIEROGLYPHICS. In this system, small pictures and symbols stood for sounds, words, and ideas. Special trained writers called scribes learned the thousands of symbols. Egyptians wrote hieroglyphics on temple walls and on PAPYRUS, an early kind of paper made from a reed plant that grew along the Nile.

For a long time, no one could read hieroglyphics. The key to unlocking them was the Rosetta Stone, a stone with the same message written in hieroglyphics and Greek, which let scholars finally translate the symbols.

The Egyptians made many other ACHIEVEMENTS. They were skilled in medicine (treating wounds and setting bones), mathematics (especially geometry), astronomy (studying the stars), and engineering. They created an accurate 365-DAY CALENDAR based on the Nile's flooding and the stars. Many of their achievements still amaze scientists today. Remember: hieroglyphics = Egypt's picture writing (NOT cuneiform, which was Sumer's).

questions.question: What early kind of paper did Egyptians write on?
questions.explanation: Egyptians wrote on papyrus made from a reed plant.

questions.question: In hieroglyphics, what did the small pictures and symbols stand for?
questions.explanation: Hieroglyphic symbols represented sounds, words, and ideas.

questions.question: Which civilization invented hieroglyphics?

questions.question: What helped scholars finally read hieroglyphics?
questions.explanation: The Rosetta Stone allowed scholars to translate hieroglyphics.

questions.question: The trained writers who learned hieroglyphics were called what?
questions.explanation: Scribes were the trained writers of Egypt.

questions.question: The Egyptians created an accurate calendar with how many days?
questions.explanation: Egyptians developed an accurate 365-day calendar.

questions.question: In which fields were the Egyptians skilled?
questions.explanation: Egyptians excelled in medicine, math, astronomy, and engineering.

questions.question: Why was inventing papyrus so useful for Egypt?

choices.B: It could be eaten as food
choices.C: It was used to build pyramids
choices.D: It gave a lighter surface to write and store records on

questions.explanation: Papyrus provided a practical surface for writing and keeping records.

questions.question: Which statement is TRUE about Egyptian achievements?

choices.B: Their 365-day calendar and medicine still impress scientists today

questions.explanation: Egyptian achievements like the calendar and medicine still amaze us today.

questions.question: Papyrus was made from what kind of plant?

choices.C: A type of grass from Greece
choices.D: A reed plant that grew along the Nile

questions.explanation: Papyrus was made from a reed plant that grew along the Nile.

questions.question: On which surfaces did Egyptians often write their hieroglyphics?
questions.explanation: Egyptians wrote hieroglyphics on temple walls and on papyrus.

questions.question: What made the Rosetta Stone so useful to scholars?

choices.B: It was the largest stone ever found
choices.D: It had the same message in hieroglyphics and Greek

questions.explanation: The Rosetta Stone had the same message in hieroglyphics and Greek, which let scholars translate the symbols.

questions.question: Egyptians based their accurate calendar on what?

questions.question: Which writing system belonged to Sumer, NOT Egypt?

questions.question: Why did it take special trained people to write hieroglyphics?

choices.A: There were thousands of symbols to learn

questions.explanation: Hieroglyphics had thousands of symbols, so trained scribes were needed to learn them.

questions.question: Setting bones and treating wounds are examples of Egyptian skill in what field?
questions.explanation: Setting bones and treating wounds are examples of Egyptian medicine.

questions.question: Which of these was NOT a field the Egyptians were skilled in?
questions.explanation: Egyptians were skilled in medicine, mathematics, astronomy, and engineering, but cars did not exist.

questions.question: Before the Rosetta Stone was understood, what was true about hieroglyphics?

choices.C: For a long time no one could read them
choices.D: They were used to count money

questions.explanation: For a long time no one could read hieroglyphics until the Rosetta Stone helped.

questions.question: Which best describes a scribe?

choices.A: A soldier who guarded the pharaoh
choices.D: A trained writer who knew hieroglyphics

questions.explanation: A scribe was a trained writer who learned the hieroglyphic symbols.

questions.question: How was a 365-day calendar helpful to Egyptian farmers?

choices.A: It told them when to expect the Nile's flooding
choices.D: It replaced the need for water

questions.explanation: The calendar helped farmers know when to expect the Nile's flooding so they could plan crops.

questions.question: Hieroglyphics and cuneiform were alike because both were what?

choices.C: Early writing systems of ancient civilizations

questions.explanation: Both hieroglyphics and cuneiform were early writing systems of ancient civilizations.

questions.question: Why is the invention of writing considered an important achievement?

choices.A: It let people record and share ideas and information
choices.C: It built the pyramids by itself

questions.explanation: Writing let people record and share ideas and information, making it an important achievement.

questions.question: Which is the BEST summary of this lesson?

choices.B: Egypt created picture writing and made advances in science and math
choices.D: Egypt copied all its ideas from Rome

questions.explanation: The lesson shows Egypt created picture writing and made advances in science and math.

questions.question: Which tool of the Egyptians shows skill in mathematics?
questions.explanation: Egyptian use of geometry shows their skill in mathematics.

questions.question: If a scientist today is impressed by the Egyptian calendar, what does that suggest?

choices.C: The Egyptians' achievement was advanced for its time

questions.explanation: A modern scientist being impressed suggests the Egyptian calendar was advanced for its time.

questions.question: Which statement about papyrus is TRUE?

choices.B: It was an early kind of paper

questions.question: Which pairing is correct?

questions.question: What did Egyptian scribes mainly do?

choices.A: Read and write the hieroglyphic symbols

questions.question: Why might temple walls covered in hieroglyphics be useful to historians today?

choices.B: They record Egyptian beliefs and history in writing

questions.explanation: Hieroglyphics on temple walls record Egyptian beliefs and history, helping historians learn about Egypt.

questions.question: Which field would an Egyptian use to study the movement of the stars?

questions.question: Compared to carving on heavy stone, why was papyrus an improvement for writing?

choices.C: It was lighter and easier to store records on

questions.question: Which of these is an example of Egyptian engineering?

questions.question: What does the word 'achievement' mean in this lesson?
questions.explanation: An achievement is a great accomplishment, like Egypt's calendar and medicine.

questions.question: Which statement is NOT true about hieroglyphics?

choices.D: They were the same thing as Sumer's cuneiform
